_comment: TEMPLATE — copy this into _data/trails/<id>.json and fill in. Delete fields you don't have data for rather than guessing; the template renders sections conditionally and skips anything empty/missing. This file is not a trek record itself — the loader only reads _data/trails/*.json.
_category_options: fort | jungle | peak-plateau | waterfall-valley | coastal | himalayan (omit category for Nepal/Himalaya treks)
name: Full Trek Name
_guideRequired_note: true for EITHER a terrain-danger judgment call (e.g. Kalavantin Durg) OR a legal requirement (Nepal conservation areas, mandatory since Apr 2023) — the FAQ builder stays generic on purpose and pulls the specific reason from gettingThere.permitNote, so put the real 'why' there, not here.
seoTitle: Trek Name Solo Trek Guide — The Solo Trail
seoDescription: One or two sentences for search results.
highlights: Optional — 3–4 short bullets shown at the top of the Overview tab
E.g. 'Permits can be arranged at the trailhead'
_highlights_gallery_note: Both fields are optional. The trail page renders the highlights box and gallery strip only if these are present. Other trails will simply skip the sections — no fallback needed.
dataNote: Optional — flag conflicting/unverified figures here, e.g. 'Altitude cited 2,700–4,350 ft across sources; using the more consistently reported figure.'
seasonNote: Optional — only needed when the prettiest season and the safest season genuinely differ, e.g. 'Prettiest in monsoon, but AMK's technical sections are safest Oct–Mar — see Safety tab.'
_routeOptions_note: Use for single/day treks with multiple approach variants. Use 'itinerary' (same shape as the Nepal treks) instead for genuine multi-day treks.

safety.intro: One or two sentences framing the real risk profile of this specific trek.

alerts.title: Named hazard
alerts.body: Specifics — where, why, what to actually do about it.

cards.title: Before you go / On the trail / Solo-specific / Signs to turn back

_logistics_note: Leave gettingThere/costs as empty objects until logistics content is ready — the template renders a 'coming soon' placeholder for empty sections instead of hiding the tab.
